sentences.text: The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ for the injuries suffered by her in a road accident dated 18.11.2020.
2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, The first respondent is the owner and second respondent is the insurer of the Santro Car bearing No.KA19MD353.
The third respondent is the is the owner and the fourth respondent is the insurer of the Mahindra XUV 500 Car bearing its Reg.No.KA01MN4693.
The petitioner is an employee in Indian Posts (Govt. Of India) as a Postal Asst. SBCO at Bangalore - 560 041.

When she was going to her on 18.11.2020 at about 9.00am by riding her Yamaha Facino Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA02JJ 0362 from Hosarodu Signal towards Kudlu Gate, near Singasandra Bus stand, a woman was crossing the Road and the driver of the Santro Car bearing REg.NO.KA10MD353 who was driving it with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering human life dashed the said women and suddenly stopped the Car and the petitioner slowdown her scooter but at the same time the driver of the Mahindra Car bearing Reg No.KA01 MN4693 who was behind her and dashed to the petitioner and she fell from the scooter and suffered injuries.
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident she was shifted to Bloossom Hospital, Bangalore and for further treatment the petitioner was shifted to Sparsh Hospital, Bangalore, treated as an inpatient from the date of accident till 23.11.2020, underwent surgeries and discharged with advice.
Before the accident she was hale and healthy, Central Government Employee , earning Rs.52,575/ per month.
Due to the injuries suffered in the accident, she suffered mentally and physically and suffering from permanent disablement.
So far she has spent huge amount towards treatment.

The Hulimavu Traffic Police have registered a criminal case against the Drivers of both the offending vehicle in Cr.No.76/2020 for the offences p/u/Sec.279, 338 of IPC and IMV Act 1988 u/Sec.135(A&B), 187, 56 & 192.
4.
In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondent Nos.1, 2 & 4 appeared, but the respondent Nos.1 & 2 filed written statements separately.
In spite of due service of notice the Respondent No.3 did not appear hence, placed exparte.

5. The objections of the Respondent No.1:
He has denied all the petition averments and stated that the Singasandra Bus stand there is slow moving traffic and no one is driving in a rash and negligent manner.
The petitioner suffered injuries due to her own negligence and the negligence of the driver of the Mahindra Car.
Further submits that his car insured with the respondent No.2.
He had a valid DL at the time of accident.
This respondent denies the huge medical expenses and the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition as against him.

sentences.text: The objections of the Respondent No.2:
It has denied all the petition averments and admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the Santro Car bearing Reg.No.KA19MD0353.
It states that the entire negligence is on the driver of the Mahindra Car because only when the Mahindra Car hits the petitioner she sustained the injuries.

There is a non compliance of Sec.134(c)
and 158(6) of MV Act.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of the petition.
7. The objections of the Respondent No.4:
It has denied all the petition averments and admitted the issuance of policy in favour of 3 rd respondent.
It has contended that there was non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The driver of the Mahindra Car have a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
The Mahindra Car was not at all involved in the accident and the entire negligence is on the part of the Santro Car.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

8. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of the Driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA19MD353 and Mahindra XUV500 Car bearing Reg.No.KA01 MN4693 and driver of Mahindra XUV 500 caused the accident to the petitioner, in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?
9. The Petitioner in order to prove her case has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.24.
In the cross examination of PW.1 by the counsel for the Respondent No.1 confronted Ex.R.1.
On the other side, the Respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 & 2.
Respondent No.4 has got examined its official as RW.2 and did not mark any documents.

10. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
11.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: In the Affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 12. Issue No.1: In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the drivers of the offending vehicles, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and produced 5 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.5.
PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the petition in her affidavit in lieu of her chief examination.
During her cross examination she has stated that there was 5 feet gap between her vehicle and the vehicle infront of her, she was at the speed of around 40km/hr.
She has stated that the car behind her hit her and in turn she fell down.

She has admitted Geetha M. Naduvinamani vs Sai Kumar P.K on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93763941/

sentences.text: She has admitted that there was no loss of pay but she lost all her ELs.
She has admitted that only Mahendra XUV Car is liable to give compensation to her.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 got examined the Administrative Officer as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 & 2.
During his cross examination he has admitted that Mahindra XUV Car did not suffer any damages.
The respondent No.4 got examined its Legal Manager as RW.2 but did not mark any documents.
During his cross examination nothing worthwhile is elicited.

13. On perusal of the FIR at Ex.P.1 it is clear that the complaint was filed on the date of accident against both Mahindra Car as well as Santro Car and the charge sheet at Ex.P.3 is filed against both the vehicles.
Ex . P.4
is the sketch, Ex.P.5 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.6 is the statement of witnesses which are all in accordance with the statement given by the complainant.
Exs. P.7, 8 & 9 are the notices given u/Sec.133 of MV Act and the reply given to the same.
Ex . P.10
is the wound certificate which shows that the petitioner suffered injuries in an RTA.
Ex . P.11
is the IMV report which shows there was damages to the Santro Car as well as Two wheeler of the petitioner but, there was no damages found on the Mahindra XUV 500.

On perusal of all the documents it is clear that the accident occurred at the first instance due to the negligence of the Santro Car and the petitioner suffered injuries only on the rash and negligence driving by the driver of the Mahindra XUV Car.
Therefore, this Tribunal holds that they are equally responsible for the injuries suffered by the petitioner and the negligence is attributed at 50% each.
Accordingly, I hold that the accident was caused due to the negligence of both the vehicles and I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:

The Petitioner has further averred that on account of the accidental injury she is suffering from grievous injuries and was treated at Blossom Hospital, Bangalore and Sparsh Hospital, Bangalore, treated as in inpatient, after surgery discharged with advice.

The Petitioner to substantiate that there is loss of income due to the accidental injuries and that she is suffering from permanent disability has not examined either the treated Doctor or any other Doctor who has got expertise in this field.
She also has not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent person to prove that she suffered permanent disability.

Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused her permanent disability resulting in loss of income and accordingly the version of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable.
Under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
However, it is pertinent to note that, the wound certificates produced as per Exs.P.10 & 15 disclose that, she has suffered grievous injuries.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,000/ under the head of Pain and Suffering.
The Petitioner has stated that she has spent Rs.5,00,000/ towards medical expenses.

In this regard she has produced 4 medical bills for Rs.1,25,089/ as per Ex.P.14, Rs.195/ at Ex.P16,
Rs.4,550/ at Ex.P.17, Rs.40,500/ at Ex.18, Rs.959/ at Ex.P.20, Rs.3,773/ at Exs.P.21 in total Rs.1,75,066/.
There is no contrary evidence to this document from the respondents.
As such, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.1,75,066/ under the head of medical expenses.

As mentioned above the Petitioner was treated at Blossom Hospital, Bangalore and Sparsh Hospital, Bangalore,
wherein she was treated as an inpatient.
In this regard she has produced Ex.P.15 discharge summary.

During that time, certainly she would have spent some amount towards attendant,
conveyance, transportation and for other incidental expenses.

In this regard she has produced Geetha M. Naduvinamani vs Sai Kumar P.K on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93763941/

sentences.text: Ambulance bills at Ex.P.24 for a sum of Rs.7,800/.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.12,000/ towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and other incidental expenses.
The total compensation comes to Rs.2,47,066/.
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.2,47,100/ Liability 15.
The Respondents did not prove their defence.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the drivers of the both Santro Car and Mahindra XUV 500 Car and they are equally liable in payment of compensation.
Hence the Respondent Nos.1 to 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/ but she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.2,47,100/ with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,47,100/ (Rupees Two Lakhs Forty Seven Thousand and One Hundred only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The Respondent Nos.2 & 4 are directed to deposit the compensation amount equally with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of epayment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
